sentence: This project tests a therapy for triple negative breast cancer that depletes copper the spreading cells rely on and alters the microenvironment tumors spread to.
This project studies how oral bacterial infections and fungal infections affect the risk that oral infections associated with cancers persist in persons living with HIV.
This project studies how a drug activates the pore-forming protein Gasdermin A and causes a form of programmed necrosis known as pyroptosis.
This project builds resources and tools to help research on the genetic and epigenetic regulation of kidney disease.
This project studies genetic variants and microbial profiles in patients with ulcerative colitis who develop Crohn's disease-like pouch inflammation after colon removal.
This project builds computer-aided tools that screen for torso hemorrhage after trauma and measure hemorrhage burden using CT angiography.
This project develops directed vascularization of bladder wall grafts as an alternative to using intestine for bladder reconstruction.
This project studies how pancreatic cancer cells use potassium channels and a calcium-handling protein to regulate nucleic acid sensing and suppress innate immune activation.
This project builds a platform to define the molecular mechanisms of microbe-microbe interactions in host-associated communities.
This project studies how molecular features of leiomyosarcoma relate to its natural history and to outcomes with systemic therapeutic agents.
This project studies how the activation of mammalian target of rapamycin contributes to the pathogenesis of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
This project uses surveys and focus groups to learn the challenges of survivors of ventilator support in an intensive care unit and creates personalized programs.
This project uses long-read sequencing to find out if gene conversion drives the diversity of resistant malaria parasites.
This project combines imaging with plasma circulating tumor DNA to monitor treatment response in patients with multiple cancers on targeted therapy.
This project uses yeast and flies to study how unique histone repertoires help with fertility, DNA damage repair and genome regulation.
This project tests antibody-drug conjugates combined with radiation therapy as a treatment for lung cancer.
This project identifies abnormal proteins that build up in multiple brain regions and single cells from Alzheimer's disease patients and checks their role in disease.
This project provides tissue culture models of digestive and liver disease by introducing specific genetic alterations into cell lines and induced pluripotent stem cells.
This project studies how uterine natural killer cells develop from peripheral blood natural killer cells into decidualized natural killer cells.
This project studies how data from registries, health systems and payers can be used to check whether cardiovascular devices are safe and effective.
